text: dsh-plugin-session-delete 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的会话管理插件：它在侧边栏会话菜单和界面浮层中提供删除操作。用户可以打开单个会话的确认对话框，也可以选择多个会话后一次确认；Host 端删除会话日志、投影缓存和工作区登记，并可将仍在使用的会话排队到下次启动处理。适合需要清理 DSH 会话记录的用户；不需要 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-plugin-session-delete adds single and bulk removal to the DSH web session menu. The Host deletes session logs, projection cache records, and workspace entries; sessions still in use can be queued for removal at the next start. No API key or external service is required.
想从 DSH 侧边栏永久移除一个不再需要的会话。
能不能一次挑选几条会话并统一确认删除？
How can I remove stored DSH sessions from the session list, including several at once?
dsh-plugin-session-delete 的功能「删除单个会话」：在侧边栏会话菜单选择删除并确认后，Host 移除会话日志、投影缓存记录和工作区登记。
dsh-plugin-session-delete 的功能「批量与延后删除」：多选会话并确认后逐项处理；仍在使用的会话可排入下次启动的清理队列。

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Why this exists：DeepSeek Harness archives sessions. Archiving is useful — the row leaves the
sidebar, the session can come back — but it is not removal. The compressed log
stays under `~/.dsh/sessions/`, the projection checkpoint stays under
`~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache/`, and the workspace keeps accounting for an
id you may never open again.

Session Delete adds the missing verb.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Why this exists：| | Archive | Delete |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Row leaves the sidebar | ✅ | ✅ |
| Conversation log on disk | stays forever | **removed** |
| Projection cache | stays | **removed** |
| Workspace accounting / pin / archive entry | kept | **removed** |
| Can be restored | unarchive | no |

Archive is untouched. Delete is a second, explicit choice at the bottom of the
same menu, behind a confirmation — one Session at a time, or several in one
pick.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Install：**Requires [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
0.2.x** (tested on `0.2.1-rc.1`). Desktop and the Web UI are both supported.

The repository is the install unit. The npm package inside it is
`dsh-plugin-session-delete`; the spec you paste is the GitHub address.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · 1. From the Plugins page (recommended)：1. Open the sidebar and choose **Plugins**.
2. Install a plugin and paste:

```text
   github:Adolanium/dsh-session-delete
   ```

3. Install it. The bundle is enabled by default.
4. Refresh the DeepSeek Harness window (`Ctrl+R` / `Cmd+R`). The browser half is
   loaded lazily, so the menu entry appears after a reload.

No build permission is needed: the package ships plain JavaScript, has no
`prepare` script, and has no runtime dependencies.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · 2. With the `dsh` CLI：If you boot profiles yourself (Web, headless, or a stopped Desktop), the same
spec installs into a named profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Adolanium/dsh-session-delete
```

`dsh` appends the bundle to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` because the
package declares `dsh.bundle`. Start DeepSeek Harness afterwards, then refresh
the window.

Pin the install if you want it frozen to this release:

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · 2. With the `dsh` CLI：```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Adolanium/dsh-session-delete#v0.2.0
```

Remove it with:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plugin-session-delete
```

> Running the CLI against the `desktop` profile while the Desktop app is running
> is supported by the profile lock, but the Plugins page is the smoother path
> there — it owns the same operation and reports activation status.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · 3. From a checkout (development)：```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Adolanium/dsh-session-delete.git
cd dsh-session-delete
pwsh -File scripts/install-dev.ps1
```

That links the checkout into `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules` and adds the
Loader entry to the profile patch (with a timestamped backup). Undo with
`scripts/uninstall-dev.ps1`.

> The profile reloads configuration live, so a linked package activates without
> a restart. HMR does not watch module roots, so **code edits need a restart**.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Use：Open a session row's **⋯** menu and choose **Delete session…**.

The dialog names the conversation and explains that the log and its cached
projections will be removed. **Delete** performs the removal; **Cancel** leaves
everything alone.

What happens next depends on the session:

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Use：| Session state | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **Cold** — no live Agent owns it | Removed immediately. The row leaves the list; the dialog closes. |
| **Live** — open in this app, or a running turn owns it | The dialog explains that the log is still in use and offers **Delete on next start**. |
| **Unknown id** | Rejected. Nothing is touched. |

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Delete on next start：A queued id whose session is already gone is dropped silently. A queued id that
is still in use stays queued for the next start.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Delete several at once：Open any row's **⋯** menu and choose **Delete multiple sessions…**.

The picker lists every Session in the catalog, newest first. It preselects the
row you opened it from, omits blank provisional rows and subagent-origin
Sessions, and offers **Select all** and **Clear**. **Delete selected (N)…** moves
to a confirmation that names the Sessions; **Delete permanently** removes the
whole selection in one Host call.

The result view reports one outcome per Session:

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Delete several at once：| Outcome | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Deleted** | The log, projection cache, and accounting are gone. |
| **Still open in the app** | A live Agent owns it. **Delete N on next start** queues the whole remainder through the same pending file. |
| **Already gone** | The id no longer resolved; the request is satisfied. |
| **Could not be removed** | A real failure (for example a storage root mismatch); its message is shown and the rest of the batch still ran. |

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Delete several at once：One action removes up to **200 Sessions**. The Host de-duplicates ids, keeps the
single-Session contract unchanged, and never lets one failed Session abort the
rest of the batch.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · What Delete removes：For each session id, the Host removes:

- **the session directory** under `~/.dsh/sessions/<project>/<session-id>/`,
  including every format generation (`session.vN.jsonl.zstd`) and the lock
  artifact;
- **the projection-cache record** from the `session_projcache` domain, through
  the domain itself, so an in-memory row cannot survive the delete;
- **the workspace accounting slot**, the global pin, and the archive entry.

It deliberately leaves:

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Safety model：Deleting a file is easy. Deleting the *right* file while the app is running is
the hard part. The plugin is built around four rules:

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Safety model：1. **One writer.** Before touching anything, the Host takes the persistence
   **write handle** for the session and immediately closes it. A live Agent,
   another DSH process, or a crashed-but-held lock makes that open fail, and the
   delete is refused. The handle is the proof of "nobody is using this". A batch
   takes that handle once per Session, so a live member never blocks the cold
   ones.
2. **Loopback only.** The route is rejected for non-loopback peers. A present
   `Origin` must be the Web client's origin or the Desktop shell's
   `dsh-app://app`; a cross-site `fetch` cannot reach it (JSON content type
   forces a preflight the route does not answer).
3. **Strict identity.** The id must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`,
   the target directory must be named exactly that id, and it must contain a
   canonical `session[.vN].jsonl[.zstd]` log. A malformed id cannot address
   another path.
4. **No surprises.** If the materialized log is not under the configured root,
   the Host refuses and says so instead of deleting accounting and leaving the
   log behind. Cleanup failures are logged; the response reports what h

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Safety model：There is no network access, no telemetry, and no background process. The plugin
reads and writes local files through the Host's own services.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Configuration：All fields are optional. Defaults match a stock installation.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dshHome` | `$DSH_HOME`, else `~/.dsh` | Data root used to derive the two roots below. |
| `sessionsRoot` | `<dshHome>/sessions` | Session persistence root — the `root` of `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`. |
| `storagesRoot` | `<dshHome>/storages` | Storage root used only as a fallback when the `storageDomain` service is absent. |

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Configuration：Set these in the profile entry if you run a non-default persistence root:

```yaml
- id: session-delete
  name: dsh-plugin-session-delete
  config:
    sessionsRoot: /srv/dsh/sessions

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Uninstall：- **Plugins page:** open the plugin and remove it.
- **CLI:** `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plugin-session-delete`.
- **Dev link:** `pwsh -File scripts/uninstall-dev.ps1`.

Queued removals stay in `~/.dsh/plugin-session-delete/pending.json`; delete that
file if you want to forget them.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · How it works：The Host half is one Cordis plugin (`lib/index.js`) that injects
`sessionPersistence` and `workspaceRegistry` and registers one exact route on
`webServer`. The browser half (`lib/client.js`) is a hand-written module-loader
bundle: two entries in `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item`, two dialogs in
`shell.overlay`, and nothing else.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Compatibility：- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.x** (tested on `0.2.1-rc.1`, Desktop and Web).
- Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- No dependencies, no build step, no native modules.
- The plugin uses public Host services (`sessionPersistence`,
  `workspaceRegistry`, `storageDomain`) and public client slots. It does not
  monkey-patch, fork, or modify DeepSeek Harness.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Compatibility：Developer preview means breaking changes. If a release moves one of those seams,
the plugin fails soft: a missing service keeps it inactive, and a failed delete
returns an error instead of half-cleaning a session.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Development：- **Host** (`test/host.test.mjs`) — the real plugin against a temporary DSH
  home, a fake persistence seam, a fake workspace registry, and direct HTTP
  request/response objects. Covers the cold/live/queued paths, batch outcomes
  and de-duplication, id and origin checks, the location guard, and the
  unarchive-cancels-removal rule.
- **Browser** (`test/client.test.mjs`) — the real `lib/client.js` loaded through
  a stub of the module-loader contract; renders both menu entries and both
  dialogs and drives the picker, confirmation, batch, and deferred flows with a
  stub `fetch`.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · Development：The artwork is generated with image models and composed with
[sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com/); the source banner lives in `assets/`.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · FAQ：**Does this replace Archive?**
No. Archive and its unarchive flow are unchanged. Delete is an additional,
explicit action.

**Can I delete several sessions at once?**
Yes. **Delete multiple sessions…** in any row's menu opens the multi-select
picker; one action removes up to 200 sessions and reports each outcome.

**Can I undo a delete?**
Not for an immediate removal. For a queued one, unarchive the session before the
next start.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · FAQ：**Why does it say the session is still open?**
The session has a live Agent in this Host. Use **Delete on next start**; the next
launch removes it.

**Why can't it find my session?**
Your persistence root is not `~/.dsh/sessions`. Set `sessionsRoot` to the `root`
used by `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`.

**Does it delete files outside `~/.dsh`?**
No. Only the session's own directory under the configured root, its
`session_projcache` record, and its registry entries.

dsh-plugin-session-delete README · FAQ：**Does it work in the browser-only Web UI?**
Yes. The browser half calls the same-origin route; the Host enforces loopback
and origin checks.
